[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, then we'll go into the APAC onramp details and the contract extension ask.

[00:29] Lina: Yep. We also want to confirm data residency and KMS details—important for compliance.
[00:34] Maya: Totally. We'll cover it, and I'll drop the security packet after the call.

[00:40] Ethan: Jumping in on the APAC pilot, from a technical view, the ask you outlined was a Japan private VPC deployment with dedicated capacity for inference and an option to burst to hosted if we hit spikes. Is that right?
[00:52] Hiro: Right. The idea is private serving in our Tokyo region for PII latency sensitive workloads, but keep the burst to Redwood-hosted for peak shopping events.
[01:00] Rajiv: And the throughput—our estimate is about 12 QPS sustained for our NER + summarization routes, with bursts up to ~60 QPS for 15 minute windows.
[01:12] Ethan: Okay that maps. For 12 QPS sustained with model size of the current LLM you run, we'd recommend a small Dedicated pool of 2 x A100-equivalent nodes with autoscale policy. The burst to hosted works but there are egress and failover policies to configure.
[01:25] Hiro: When you say A100-equivalent, are you recommending Redwood Dedicated physical hosts or cloud equivalents? We prefer something we can control.
[01:32] Ethan: Good question—by default Dedicated is a Redwood-managed reserved pool in the region. For the private pilot we can do Customer-Managed VPC peering + private control plane; if you need full on-prem we can discuss — that's a different SOW.
[01:44] Lina: We wanted to understand latency SLOs. Right now our internal target is p95 < 220ms for short chat-like prompts. Can you meet that in Tokyo region?
[01:54] Ethan: For short sequences and optimized kernels, on Dedicated yes, p95 of ~150-220ms is realistic. If you use batching for cost savings, that's where latency lifts. There's the latency vs cost tradeoff.
[02:07] Rajiv: We're sensitive to cost, but user experience matters. Can you show the cost delta between hosted with aggressive batching vs dedicated without batching?
[02:16] Maya: We'll put a cost comparison in the updated proposal—rough numbers: hosted with batching reduces per-token cost by ~40% but p95 increases ~80-120ms depending on batch windows. Dedicated with tuned batching can still be competitive.
[02:30] Amara: On procurement, we need a 12 month extension and clarity on termination clauses for the pilot. Also want a price lock for 12 months for committed units.
[02:40] Maya: We can do a 12-month amendment, price lock on committed capacity, add a pilot clause for APAC private deployment with an acceptance criteria. We'll capture fallback to hosted and burst egress billing.

[02:51] Ethan: Small note on fallback: our routing policy can fallback to smaller quantized variants if Dedicated is saturated. Quality delta is visible in some prompt families, so we usually tie that to canary rules and an automatic notify.
[03:04] Rajiv: That's fine as long as we get a rollback plan and eval metrics. We'll bring our eval prompt suite to the benchmark.
[03:11] Hiro: For network, we need details on VPC peering, IP ranges, and certificate exchange—can you share the template?
[03:18] Ethan: Yes, we'll share the VPC peering template and an IP allowlist window.
[03:22] Maya: I'll attach that with the security packet.

[03:28] Lina: On encryption—KMS integration is a must. We use a cloud KMS, and for key custody we need HSM-backed options.
[03:36] Maya: Redwood supports KMS integration; we have HSM-backed options for Private. We'll include the KMS architecture doc in the security pack.
[03:44] Amara: Also SOC 2 and ISO evidence for audits. We've got to run our vendor checklist.
[03:49] Sofia (CSM): We already have an abbreviated SOC2 summary in our portal; we'll push the full package and SOC2 report after NDA.
[03:57] Lina: Great. Also SSO—SAML is our preference, role-based access control and audit logs for token-level tracing.
[04:05] Ethan: All supported—RBAC, token tracing, per-route logs. Small caveat: token-level cost breakdown in the dashboard may show approximate mapping for cached prefixes.
[04:16] Rajiv: Speaking of caching, we rely on prefix caching to control cost. Any limits on KV cache size per session?
[04:23] Ethan: There's a configurable KV cache; we usually set a per-request KV cache limit. For long chat sessions the KV cache memory footprint can be tuned and we've got quantization recommendations.
[04:33] Rajiv: Ok. Can you run a sample with our 10k prompt replay and show token-level cost?
[04:38] Ethan: Yes, that's in the perf plan. We'll ask you to share the sample dataset and we'll run the replay on a staging model.

[04:45] Amara: Back to contracting—what's the uplift cost for Dedicated capacity in Tokyo vs general hosted? We need to present to finance.
[04:54] Maya: I'll outline a couple of options in the proposal: committed reserved pool (best unit price) vs committed plus burst credits (middle ground) vs hosted-only (no infra commitment). Each has different egress/peering charges; we'll quantify.
[05:06] Hiro: Are there any compliance constraints that would prevent Redwood from peering into our VPC?
[05:11] Ethan: For VPC peering there's no data plane copy—traffic flows over private link. For stricter controls we can do an on-prem appliance or air-gapped approach but that's a heavier lift.
[05:21] Lina: We're also worried about failover—if Tokyo Dedicated goes down, can we fail to a Singapore region?
[05:27] Ethan: Yes, geo-failover can route to another region; be aware of residency/regulatory constraints. We can set automatic fallback to Singapore hosted or to your preferred region.

[05:36] Rajiv: For the perf benchmark, we want to see: latency p50/p95, throughput sustained at target QPS, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regression metrics on our eval prompts.
[05:47] Ethan: We'll produce a perf runbook: test checklist, timeline, required credentials, and expected sample outputs.
[05:53] Maya: OK let's align on dates — Rajiv, do you think you can provide the prompt replay and sample traffic pattern by Monday (2026-11-16)?
[06:01] Rajiv: Yes that's doable, we'll anonymize and send over.
[06:04] Amara: Procurement will need the final amendment to review by 2026-11-20 to sign before month-end.
[06:10] Maya: We'll aim to get the proposal and draft amendment to you by 2026-11-16 so you have a few days.

[06:16] Lina: A couple of clarifying points — if you quantize to reduce model size for cost, can we opt-out for certain critical routes?
[06:23] Ethan: Yes, per-route model pinning is supported; you can pin critical routes to high-quality variants and allow other routes to use cheaper quantized models.
[06:32] Rajiv: Any mention of competitor or vendor lock? We evaluate ZephyrAI and a few others.
[06:36] Maya: We discussed vendor-neutral model catalog; you won't be locked to a single variant — but note that some optimizations are runtime-specific. We'll document portability caveats.

[06:45] Sofia: Quick ops note — for billing we'll include a breakout: committed units, burst credits used, egress/peering fees, and optional premium SLA.
[06:54] Amara: Sounds good. One more ask: can you include a trial of per-route A/B rollout for 2 weeks so we can measure quality delta?
[07:02] Maya: Yes we can include a 2-week canary roll for the pilot, with automatic rollback on quality regression thresholds.
